name: INTELLECT EATER

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Intellect Eater

The dreaded intellect eater has been a scourge in
recent days and victims of these parasites have been
turning up in the Confederacy’s lands, especially in
the client villages and towns who support the larger
cities. Intellect eaters infest sewers and enter their
victims’ bodies through the openings of their sexual
organs and conceal their entry with the anesthetizing
slime their thin bodies exude.
Once inside the host, the eater coils around its
victim’s spine, where it remains dormant for a full year,
feeding on the host’s spinal fluid, while it grows ever
larger. When it reaches adulthood, the worm chews a
hole out from the base of its host’s throat. Fully sentient,
when the intellect eater partly emerges from the host, it
takes control of the host’s body and can communicate
using the host’s mouth and vocal cords.

Intellect Eater Effects
Infection A creature that moves through a fluid infested
with intellect eaters, such as in a pit underneath an
outhouse or a city sewer might become infected by
the parasite. Roll a d6. On a 6, the parasite invades the
host’s body by way of its genitals. While infected, the
host creature makes Agility attack rolls and challenge
rolls with 1 bane and grants 1 boon on attack rolls made
against its Agility. One year after infection, the worm
reaches maturity with the following effects.
A mature intellect eater shares control of the host
body until the host body dies, which kills the parasite as
well. The eater uses the following statistics.

INTELLECT EATER

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1/8 horrifying monster
Perception 15 (+5); darksight
Defense *; Health *; Insanity 0; Corruption 4
Strength 5 (–5), Agility 5 (–5), Intellect 12 (+2), Will 13 (+3)
Speed 2
Shared Defense and Health The intellect eater uses the
host’s Defense and Health scores. The intellect eater can
also use the host’s Strength and Agility in place of its
own for as long as it resides in the host’s body.

Immune dazed, stunned
Parasite The intellect eater resides inside of its host’s body.
If the host dies, so too does the intellect eater. The eater
can use an action once per round, taking its turn when
its host does. The parasite uses its host’s body to resolve
the use of its action.

Mind Fire
It takes just one of these amorphous microorganisms
entering the body for it to wreak havoc. The
organism moves through its host along its blood
stream until it takes root in the brain, where it
remains, eating away at the gray matter until it is so
full of holes the victim dies. The infection causes
derangement, erratic behavior, and violent outbursts.
Victims of mind fire run a low fever and blood pools
in the sclera of their eyes.
Surgery The organism grows larger as it feeds on
its victim’s brain and its wet, slippery, formless body
fills in the holes that it creates. A victim at Stage 3
or higher might be rescued from the disease as the
parasite is of a size large enough to be surgically
extracted. A healer or surgeon can make the attempt,
which requires sawing away a portion of the skull
and rooting around inside the brain to reveal the
creature from the brain tissue its body has replaced.
Then, it’s just a matter of tongs and a firm grip to
remove it.
A creature who undergoes this surgery takes a
permanent 1d3 penalty to its Intellect score and
gains 1d6 Insanity, which cannot be reduced by
any means.

Mind Fire Effects
Infection The next time a creature who consumes
contaminated water or food completes a rest, the
creature must make a Strength challenge roll with 2 banes.
On a failure, the creature suffers the effects of stage
1 infection. While infected, the creature is diseased
and, each time it completes a rest, must make another
Strength challenge roll with 2 banes. Find the results of
the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from mind fire and becomes
immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature makes Will challenge rolls with 2 banes.
Stage 2 As stage 1, and the creature gains 1d6 Insanity.
If the creature becomes subject to madness, do not roll
on the Madness table. Instead, the creature becomes
subject to Violence.
Stage 3 As stage 1, and the creature gains 2d6 Insanity.
If the creature becomes subject to madness, do not roll
on the Madness table. Instead, the creature becomes
subject to Violence and rolls twice, using the lower
result, to end the madness effect.
Stage 4 The creature takes damage equal to its Health
and a mind fire slime slithers out from its nostrils. The
creature is hostile to all creatures and takes the next
available turn to attack the creature nearest to it.
Aftereffects The creature’s maximum amount of Insanity
is permanently reduced by 2.

--- PDF p. 4 ---

name: MIND FIRE SLIME

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
MIND FIRE SLIME

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1/2 frightening ooze
Perception 10 (+0); sightless
Defense 8; Health 33; Insanity —; Corruption 0
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 8 (–2), Intellect 5 (–5), Will 15 (+5)
Speed 6; climber, swimmer
Immune damage from disease; blinded, charmed, dazed,
diseased, frightened, grabbed, prone, stunned, and any
effect that would change its shape.
Infectious Any living creature of flesh and blood that
touches or is touched by the mind fire slime becomes
exposed to mind fire.
Confounding Thoughts The mind fire slime broadcasts
the thoughts of creatures whose brains it has devoured.
At the end of each round, each creature within short
range of the slime must succeed on a Will challenge roll
with 1 bane or gain 1 Insanity. A successful challenge roll
renders the creature immune to this slime’s confounding
thoughts until the creature completes a rest.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Pseudopod (melee) +1 with 3 boons (2d6)

Nerothian
Fungal Spores

Like the rot maiden, the nerothian fungus too has
a humanoid shape, but rather than attaining that
shape by growth, the form comes from the creature
victimized by its spores. Nerothian fungus thrives
when it grows in rotting meat, and from the inverted
caps that unfold all over the body waft millions
of spores drifting in the breeze and searching for
purchase on the body of a nearby creature.
So small are these motes that they can lodge in skin
pores and take root, tendrils spreading throughout the
body to control the host’s nervous system. After a few
days, the fungus makes its host into something like a
zombie, until the body finally gives out and dies.
Immolation Fire destroys the fungus’s spores
and thus the only real cure for this infestation is to
burn the victim alive or near enough that the spores
die while leaving the host creature a burned ruin.
A creature infected with the spores that becomes
incapacitated by damage from fire and at least half the
damage in its damage total comes from fire is cured of
the infection.

Nerothian Fungal Spores Effects
Infection A corpse of a creature that succumbed to the
spore infection emits spores that partially obscure a
sphere of space with a 5-yard radius centered on a
point in the corpse’s space. Any creature that enters the
area of spores becomes infected. A creature with fur
covering its body can roll a d20 and escapes infection
on a roll of 10 or higher. A creature infected in this way
suffers the stage 1 effects of the parasites 24 hours later.
Henceforth, whenever the infected creature completes a
rest, it must make a Strength challenge roll with 3 banes.
Find the results of the roll below.
• Success, 20 or higher Reduce the infection stage by one.
• Success No change.
• Failure Increase the infection stage by one.
• Failure, 0 or lower Increase the infection stage by two.
Stage 0 The creature recovers from the nerothian fungal
spores and becomes immune to it for 24 hours.
Stage 1 The creature is diseased.
Stage 2 As stage 1, but the creature is also impaired and
slowed.
Stage 3 As stage 2, but whenever the creature gets a
failure on an attack roll or challenge roll, the creature
becomes controlled by the GM for 1d3 rounds.
Stage 4 The creature becomes a fungal thrall of its Size
and stops making Strength challenge rolls to fight the
infection. The creature remains a fungal thrall until it dies.
Apply the following template to the creature.

FUNGAL THRALL

DIFFICULTY REDUCE BY ONE

fungus
Perception 10 (+0); sightless
Insanity —; Corruption —
Intellect —, Will —
Speed 6
Immune asleep, blinded, dazed, deafened, fatigued,
frightened, stunned
Fungal Control Unless attacked, in which case it defends
itself, the fungal thrall takes a fast turn each round and
moves its Speed in a randomly determined direction.
Infectious Spores When a creature that can reach the
fungal thrall deals damage to it with a melee weapon,
the attacking creature must succeed on an Intellect
challenge roll or become infected with the spores as
described above.

MAGIC
Power 0
The creature loses all traditions and spells.
Aftereffects When attacked by a fungus, the creature
grants the attacking creature 1 boon on its attack roll.
